body:
The story starts a bit back with a change in my medications. I was originally taking Concerta (methylphenidate) for my ADHD, but then switched to a therapist who "could not prescribe stimulants", ergo I ended up with Strattera (atomoxetine). I took it for the first time the day after it was prescribed and it almost immediately caused issues.
Around 30 minutes after I took it I was driving and already started to feel the effects. It helped me focus, but less in the way that it made me want to focus and more in the way that I felt like if I didn't focus I was going to die. I felt my palms get sweaty, and started to breathe faster and harder. My heart felt as if it were going to explode, and I eventually had to let someone else take over the drivers seat.
About an hour in it started to feel like I couldn't breathe, and I started to cry which hasn't happened due to a medication since I was prescribed Vyvanse (lisdexamfetamine) when I was about 8 years old. It was an extreme sense of anxiety that something was about to happen, I just didn't know what.
About 30 minutes later (an hour and a half in) the negative effects started to subside and at the 2 hour mark they were gone entirely, but I had also lost the entire focus boost I had at first. I just felt sleepy and kind of sick from it. This experience made me stop taking the pill entirely.
Conclusion: I miss my diet meth. Strattera isn't fun and I cant even sell it. FML.
